summary:
Turkey's national framework governs Ordu Province, and no local measure, enforcement programme or institution concerning trans visitors is recorded for Ordu in this edition's sources. What a trans visitor to Ordu faces is the national picture alone.

Amnesty International's Türkiye country report (Report 2025/26), covering the national situation applying to every province including Ordu, records that in June 2025 authorities issued blanket bans against the Istanbul LGBTI and Trans pride marches, police subjected peaceful protesters to unlawful use of force, and over 90 people were arbitrarily detained. Prosecutions of 92 people for participating in pride marches continued at year's end. In December 2025 an İzmir court ordered the dissolution of the Young LGBTI+ Association after ruling it had shared 'obscene' images incompatible with 'society's moral values'.

Amnesty records that three draft law packages targeting LGBTI people were made public during 2025, an unprecedented assault that would criminalise expression of LGBTI identities and consensual same-sex relations and make legal gender recognition nearly impossible. The packages were ultimately not submitted to parliament.
tangentialFactors:
The draft packages' provisions on legal gender recognition, had they advanced, would have directly affected trans visitors presenting identity documents; their non-submission leaves the existing recognition regime in place for now, though whether they will be reintroduced is unresolved in the sources.

Amnesty's documentation of pride-march bans and mass detentions in Istanbul and the İzmir court's dissolution order concern other provinces, but they indicate the national enforcement climate a trans visitor to Ordu would also stand under.
localsOnly: Homosexuality has been legal in Turkey since the Ottoman penal code of 1958, and Turkey's national framework governs Ordu Province. No Ordu-specific enforcement programme, institution or local measure concerning trans residents is recorded in this edition's sources.
outOfScopeNotes:
No usable Ordu-specific finding is available in this edition's sources; the province record rests entirely on the national layer carried by the parent dossier.

Whether the three 2025 draft law packages will be resubmitted to parliament is unresolved in the sources.
